title: The Army That Lost a War to Birds 🐦 #shorts
hook: An army lost a war… to birds.
cast: a serious army major with a big curly moustache, 1930s khaki Australian army uniform and a slouch hat

lines.say: In 1932, an army went to war against birds. And the birds won.
shots: a huge flock of emus charging across a dry wheat field toward tiny soldiers, dust clouds, epic
close-up of a smug emu with big eyes staring at the camera

lines.say: After World War One, soldiers in Western Australia were given land to grow wheat.
shots: a small farmhouse with golden wheat fields under a big blue Australian sky
a farmer in a hat proudly holding a bundle of wheat

lines.say: Then around twenty thousand emus arrived, and started eating and trampling the crops.
shots: thousands of emus stampeding through golden wheat, wheat flying everywhere
the farmer pulling his hair in despair while emus eat his wheat around him

lines.say: So the government sent the army. Two soldiers, two machine guns, and Major Meredith.
shots: {hero} saluting next to a vintage army truck with a mounted gun, two soldiers beside him
{hero} looking through binoculars across the dry outback, determined face

lines.say: But the emus split into small groups and ran in every direction, at up to fifty kilometres an hour.
shots: emus scattering in every direction across red dusty outback, soldiers confused in the middle
the army truck bouncing over rough ground chasing a single emu, gun shaking

lines.say: The guns jammed. The trucks could not keep up. After about a month, the army gave up.
shots: {hero} holding a jammed smoking gun, emus laughing in the background
the army truck stuck in mud, soldiers pushing it while emus watch

lines.say: The Major later said that with emus' toughness, he could face any army in the world.
shots: {hero} standing at attention speaking to reporters with old cameras, thoughtful face
a proud emu wearing a tiny medal, standing on a hill at sunset

lines.say: Humans, zero. Emus, one. Would you have bet on the birds?
shots: a scoreboard style scene with a tiny soldier on one side and a giant emu on the other
a flock of emus walking off into the sunset across the outback

description:
In 1932 Australia sent soldiers with machine guns to fight emus eating farmers' wheat. The emus won. A true story: the Great Emu War.

Sources: National Museum of Australia; Wikipedia: Emu War.

Made with AI-assisted pictures and voice.
